item.title: NFL Makes Unusual Officiating Move Amid Growing Scrutiny
item.description: The NFL has moved referee Alex Moore’s crew off Sunday Night Football after disputed calls in the Week 7 Green Bay Packers- Detroit Lions game drew scrutiny. The change comes on the heels of last week’s controversial matchup between the Packers and the Lions, which ignited heavy debate across the league. Officials shifted away from primetime to prevent on-air scrutiny Moore’s crew will officiate the Patriots-Dolphins game in CBS’s 4:25 p.m. ET window next Sunday. Hochuli’s crew will work Eagles-Commanders on NBC at 8:20 p.m. The teams keep their scheduled matchups; only the crews change. Dec 30, 2024; Santa Clara, California, USA; San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (13) is congratulated by teammates after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter against the Detroit Lions at Levi’s Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images Football Zebras reported that , “The switch is more about optics rather than a disciplinary action.” The report did not include a public explanation from the NFL. The disputed calls included two roughing-the-passer flags against the Packers. Karl Brooks was penalized on the Lions’ final drive after Jared Goff completed an 18-yard pass to Sam LaPorta. The 15-yard flag put the Lions at the Packers’ 45. Packers safety Xavier McKinney criticized the officials after the loss in a postgame callout . The two calls brought the Packers’ roughing-the-passer total to eight through seven games; opponents had not drawn one. Brenton Cox Jr. drew a second disputed roughing penalty after being blocked directly into Goff, while Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes was flagged for a questionable illegal hit on a defenseless player – a series of rulings that severely compounded the Packers’ challenges. Moore later told a pool reporter he could not confirm whether a whistle had sounded. LaFleur asked for consistent calls in his postgame remarks. The controversial rulings intensified postgame frustrations, with Packers coach Matt LaFleur calling for consistency and safety Xavier McKinney heavily criticizing the officiating. Raiders minority owner and Fox analyst Tom Brady heavily criticized the officiating during the late-window Packers-Lions clash, putting a national spotlight on the crew’s mistakes before a massive television audience. ProFootballTalk’s Mike Florio argued that moving Moore’s crew off Sunday Night Football could keep NBC commentators Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth from revisiting the flags. That was Florio’s analysis, not a stated league reason. item.title: Packers’ Christian Watson Steps Out of Ambulance After Hospital Clearance to Post Career-High 113 Yards
item.description: The Green Bay Packers entered Thursday Night Football hoping to bounce back from a 20-17 loss at the Detroit Lions. Wide receiver Christian Watson was playing like their best weapon against the Carolina Panthers in the first half. Then one hard fall at Lambeau Field quickly changed the mood of the night, and what followed left even veteran NFL insiders talking. Christian Watson Returns to Packers Game After Leaving in Ambulance Watson went down midway through the second quarter after a 53-yard catch from Jordan Love . He battled between two defenders, landed hard on the turf and stayed down. Panthers cornerback Will Lee was shaken up on the play too. The WR walked off under his own power, and the Packers listed him as questionable with a chest injury. Soon after, Prime Video cameras showed him climbing into an ambulance. Reporter Kaylee Hartung said he was going to a hospital for precautionary reasons. Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson (9) laughs during practice on Tuesday, June 2, 2026, at the Don Hutson Center in Ashwaubenon, Wis. Tork Mason/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin The scare felt serious. Watson had already caught six passes for 100 yards on seven targets, and the Packers could not afford to lose him. Following halftime, the Packers confirmed that Watson had passed his tests at the hospital and was returning to the stadium. He walked out of the ambulance and rejoined the game in the third quarter, with Green Bay holding a 20-10 lead. Ari Meirov described the moment on X , “The closest thing to a WWE script I’ve ever seen in the NFL.” Christian Watson has popped back out of the ambulance after a trip to the hospital and is going to return tonight. The closest thing to a WWE script I’ve ever seen in the NFL. https://t.co/NLFawiPktI — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 30, 2026 But this was not Watson’s first hospital scare, and the backstory shows why Green Bay leans on him so heavily. Watson’s big contract and breakout season Watson has been here before. After a 34-26 loss to the Denver Broncos last December, he went to a hospital with a chest and shoulder injury, flew home with the team and still played the following Saturday at Chicago. “I was just mad that I had to be doing this when we’ve got a game going on,” Watson said afterward. The Packers backed him in June with a four-year extension reportedly worth $110.5 million. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported a $31 million signing bonus as part of it. Some fans blasted the price tag at first, yet Watson has kept producing. Before Thursday, he led the team with 34 catches, 595 yards and six touchdowns. Those numbers made the scare on Thursday even harder to watch. Green Bay improved to 5-3 with a 27-19 win, while Carolina fell to 3-4. Next up for the Packers is a trip to face the New England Patriots on Nov. 8. New England is 4-3 and visits Miami first. item.title: Nick Saban Explains Why Ohio State’s Backup Quarterback Doesn’t Need to Be a Hero vs. USC
item.description: The Ohio State Buckeyes face a quarterback change ahead of their USC matchup after Julian Sayin suffered an injury against Indiana. With two backups available to replace him, Nick Saban has shared what the Buckeyes need from their next starting quarterback. Nick Saban’s advice for Ohio State’s backup against USC Nick Saban has shared his expectations for Ohio State’s backup quarterback ahead of the USC matchup. Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, Saban said the replacement does not need to win the game on his own. Instead, he needs to play efficiently, make good decisions and avoid mistakes that could cost the team. Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin (10) leaves the field in a sling following the 19-15 win over the Indiana Hoosiers in the NCAA football game at Memorial Stadium Stadium in Bloomington, Ind. on Oct. 17, 2026. “I don’t think this quarterback needs to win the game for them. He just needs to be efficient and effective enough not to lose it,” Saban said. Ohio State will face USC without starting quarterback Julian Sayin, who suffered an injury during the October 17 game against Indiana. He remains sidelined indefinitely, leaving the Buckeyes to choose between two backup options Before his injury, Sayin recorded 2,007 passing yards, 19 touchdowns and four interceptions in seven games. Ohio State will enter the game without its leading passer as the team prepares for the road matchup. True freshman Luke Fahey and redshirt freshman Tavien St. Clair are the two candidates to replace Sayin. Fahey has recorded 203 passing yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions this season. St. Clair has completed five of seven passes for 52 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Neither backup has extensive experience leading Ohio State’s offense. Both could have an opportunity to take on a larger role in the upcoming matchup. The No. 2-ranked Buckeyes enter the USC game with a 6–1 record. They average 39.3 points per game and allow 13.4 points per game on defense. Those numbers give the team production on both sides of the ball entering the matchup. Ohio State also has established offensive contributors. Wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has recorded 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns this season. Running back Bo Jackson has added 516 rushing yards, giving the offense another option alongside its passing attack. USC enters the October 31 matchup with a 6–2 record. The teams will meet at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava has thrown for 2,303 yards and 19 touchdowns this season. With Sayin unavailable, Fahey or St. Clair will have to lead Ohio State’s offense against USC. The Buckeyes enter the matchup with established contributors on both sides of the ball as they adjust at quarterback. item.title: Derry fight back to draw with Sligo in final league game
item.description: Teenager Doherty scored a late double to rescue a point for Derry [Getty Images] A much-changed Derry City side fought back to draw 2-2 against relegated Sligo Rovers in their final Premier Division game of the season. First-half goals from Gareth McElroy and Ryan O'Kane gave the hosts a comfortable advantage at the break. Kaiyne Woolery was shown a red card soon after the restart and Derry made their numerical advantage count, with 17-year-old Terence Doherty scoring a late double to rescue a point. The Candystripes finished the season in fifth, with 48 points from their 36 games. Their focus will now switch to their FAI Cup final against Waterford at Aviva Stadium on Sunday, 8 November. Captain McElroy opened the scoring on 25 minutes at the Showgrounds, firing home his second goal of the season after Derry failed to clear their lines from a free-kick. O'Kane added a second on 37 minutes with a fine strike before Woolery was dismissed just three minutes into the second half. Youngster Doherty scored on 77 minutes to reduce the deficit and followed that up with his and his team's second with a header five minutes later to equalise.

It’s proved a game-changer in terms of how New England prepare, develop and recruit players, along with significant other investments in medical staff, travel and the player care department, which assist both the athletes and their families with off-field logistics. item.description: Competing on their home dirt at the Gans Creek Cross Country Course, the Missouri men’s and women’s cross country teams surged to dual top-four team postseason performances Friday morning at the 2026 SEC Championships. In front of a vocal home crowd along the Gans Creek stretch, the Mizzou women secured an impressive fourth-place team finish in a stacked 16-team field, while the Mizzou men took fourth place overall in their 14-team championship 8,000-meter race. “They’ve really come together in the last few weeks and I think for all of us, it’s exciting, but it’s a little bit of a deep breathe as well to know that, what we believe about ourselves, we can go back that up with performance,” head distance coach Kyle Levermore said. Alabama captured the women’s team title with 48 points, while the Crimson Tide men also swept the team crown with 37 points. Wanjiku lead women’s fourth-place finish In the morning’s opening 6K race, sophomore Monica Wanjiku paced the Tigers with an elite front-running effort, crossing the finish line with a new personal best of 19:05.2 to claim seventh place overall and lead Mizzou’s scoring attack. Her result secured All-SEC First Team honors for the second year in a row and was nearly a full minute faster than her time of 20:02.2 from last year’s conference meet. “I always tell myself, even if the pain comes, you have to go through it,” Wanjiku said. “Some people feel pain, but they feel like, oh I want to give up. But the moment you feel that pain, that’s when the race is starting. So, you have to keep on pushing.” Following Wanjiku, Kobi Walker turned in a strong performance to finish 17th overall with her new personal best of 19:27.2. Charlotte Cullen rounded out Mizzou’s top five scorers in 55th place with a time of 20:35.4. The Tigers posted a team score of 138 points to lock down fourth place, finishing ahead of regional powerhouses such as Arkansas, Kentucky, and Oklahoma. item.title: El Barça resiste ante un Valencia Basket combativo y sella una victoria de carácter (98-94)
item.description: El Barça resiste ante un Valencia Basket combativo y sella una victoria de carácter (98-94) El Barça supera a un Valencia Basket muy combativo en el Palau y suma una victoria de carácter en un duelo de máxima exigencia. El Barça sacó adelante un exigente duelo ante el Valencia Basket (XX-XX) en el Palau Blaugrana. Los azulgranas encontraron en Joel Parra y Kevin Punter a dos de sus grandes referentes para resistir ante un rival muy combativo y cerrar una victoria de carácter en la Euroliga. El Barça comenzó el partido a base de triples. Punter, Robinson y Parra encadenaron aciertos desde el perímetro para situar el 8-9, antes de que Punter volviera a aparecer con dos triples consecutivos para ampliar la ventaja azulgrana (19-11). El escolta azulgrana, en estado de gracia, alcanzó los nueve puntos en apenas cinco minutos, con tres triples anotados. Armoni Brooks respondió con un 2+1, pero el arreón culé obligó al Valencia a pedir tiempo muerto. Un robo de Umude y dos puntos de Brizuela al contraataque ampliaron la diferencia (23-14), aunque Corbalán respondió desde el perímetro. En medio del vendaval ofensivo azulgrana, Mouhamadou Gueye mantuvo a flote al conjunto valenciano con dos tapones. El Barça, sin embargo, no bajó el ritmo y supo responder a cada canasta rival. Dos puntos de Nkamhoua sobre la bocina devolvieron a los azulgranas una ventaja de cinco puntos al término del primer cuarto (30-25). La defensa marca un segundo cuarto de máxima tensión El segundo periodo arrancó con una mayor intensidad defensiva por parte de ambos equipos. item.title: Giants Burn $10 Million On Darnell Mooney As Rookie Takes Over
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images The New York Giants lit $3 million on fire when they signed Darnell Mooney. This deal was supposed to bring a veteran leader to help Malik Nabers. The team thought Mooney could fix their depth issues after letting go of older receivers. That plan has fallen apart in the first seven weeks of the 2026 season. Mooney signed a one-year deal worth up to $10 million. He hoped to revive his career after a rough year in Atlanta. The Giants wanted him to be their second-best receiver. GMEN HQ reported that the team was desperate for depth behind Nabers. They thought his past work with Matt Nagy in Chicago would help. But the results on the field tell a different story. Stats Do Not Lie Through the first seven weeks, Mooney has caught just nine passes. He has gained 113 yards and has three carries for 32 yards. He is healthy and has a clear path to start. Yet, he has been outperformed by players with much less experience. Josh Cuevas, Efton Chism, Dohnte Meyers, Konata Mumpfield, Elijah Higgins, and Jordan Watkins have all caught more passes than him. The Giants only guaranteed him $3 million. So, the financial hit is not total. But the opportunity cost is high. The team needed a reliable target who could gain 500 or 600 yards. Mooney has not come close to that mark. There is no room for him in the long-term plans anymore. He is now a stain on what was a good free agent class. The Rise of Malachi Fields A younger option is now getting the trust of the coaches. Rookie wideout Malachi Fields has started to shine in recent weeks. During the 27-21 overtime victory over the Houston Texans, Fields caught four of his five targets. He gained 83 yards and had a huge 47-yard catch-and-run. Quarterback J.J. McCarthy threw him the ball perfectly. Fields is bigger than Mooney at 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds. He is also a better red-zone threat and a willing run blocker. The rookie is almost six years younger than the 29-year-old veteran. If the Giants want a WR2 to grow with this offense, the choice is clear. GMEN HQ noted that Fields has made the most of his chances when they come. A Costly Lesson for the Front Office The signing was a low-stakes deal, but it failed to produce. Mooney caught just one pass for four yards in the win over Houston. That is a sign of a player who could be on the roster bubble.

item.title: Cardinals Must Decide On Ryne Stanek’s $6 Million Option Now
item.description: John Hefti-Imagn Images The St. Louis Cardinals have a tight deadline to make a big choice about their bullpen. The World Series ended on Wednesday night, and the team now has until Monday, Nov. 2 to act. For the 2027 season, the team must evaluate a $6 million club option for veteran reliever Ryne Stanek, according to Yahoo Sports. This is not a small decision for a team looking to fix its biggest weakness. Stanek pitched in 70 games for the Cardinals this past year. He logged a 4.02 ERA and finished with a 65-to-32 strikeout-to-walk ratio over 62 2/3 innings. While he struggled early on, he turned things around for the rest of the year. In 56 total appearances spanning April 30 until the season’s conclusion, Stanek recorded a 2.84 ERA. That late-season run was strong enough to keep fans hoping for his return. The Price Tag Problem Money is the main reason the Cardinals might walk away from the deal. Spotrac projects Stanek’s market value to be just over $3.4 million for a one-year deal. That number is half of what the club option costs. Paying a 35-year-old reliever $6 million seems like a bad move for a team that wants to rebuild. The gap between the option price and the market rate is too wide to ignore. Even though Stanek was a good addition, the cost is just too high. He appeared in just under half of St. Louis’ games, and the Cardinals relied on him heavily all year. But a $6 million price point is likely too much for a veteran who might struggle with age. The team needs to find cheaper ways to shore up the bullpen this winter. Why He Was Worth Keeping The case for keeping Stanek is not based on his start to the season. In his first 14 appearances, he logged a 9.00 ERA in just 12 innings pitched. That start was ugly, but the team still won 11 of those 14 games. It shows the bullpen was not the only problem, and Stanek was not the sole reason for early losses. He was a good addition for the Cardinals overall. His ability to get outs when the game mattered most cannot be overlooked. If the Cardinals decline the option, they should not end the conversation. A lower price point, such as the projected $3.4 million, is an option they can explore for Stanek’s return. That would be a fair deal for both sides. Stanek would get paid what he is worth, and the team would get a solid arm without the huge cost. The Path Forward While the Cardinals’ bullpen served as the club’s biggest weakness in 2026, Stanek wasn’t the problem. He was one of the few bright spots in a shaky season. The team needs to fix the bullpen this winter, and bringing Stanek back could be one way to help. But only if the money is right. The front office has five days to make a call that could save millions or secure a reliable arm.

item.title: Islam Makhachev reveals UFC timeline, addresses Carlos Prates vs. Michael Morales

UFC 336: Why Islam Makhachev’s absence doesn’t warrant interim title The fight itself is phenomenal and will guarantee fireworks, but the interim title attached to it is odd, to say the least. Makhachev fought two months ago, at UFC 330 in August. Interim titles are meant for when a champion is injured or severely inactive; Makhachev fits neither category. Sure, he’s not the most active, fighting about once every nine months. That said, Makhachev isn’t holding up the division by any means, which makes the interim title feel cheap here. Makhachev has received a ton of criticism since the booking; some of it is warranted. After UFC 330, Makhachev was adamant that he wanted to fight before Ramadan, staying active since he’s not getting any younger. Now he’s opting to wait until after Ramadan, which goes against what he said just months ago. The inconsistency in his timeline is especially notable here. Speaking on Friday, Makhachev defended his patience and explained why Carlos Prates and Michael Morales need to fight before he returns. item.description: Colton Herta has finally achieved the F1 super license after his FP1 outing at the Mexico GP, amid rumors of a Cadillac seat in 2027. It didn’t look likely at the start of the 2026 F1 season, but now, at the far end of the year, there is a chance that Herta could be an F1 driver in 2027 if Cadillac pulls the plug. Amid a dismal Formula 2 (F2) season, the American has something to cheer about. A string of FP1 sessions in 2026 helped him finally secure the F1 super license, which thwarted his earlier F1 chance four years ago. A move to F2 from IndyCar was carved out to help him score the required points, which required him to finish well inside the Top 10. However, the F2 season with Hitech GP has been far from convincing, as it has been a difficult run. Cadillac took the alternate route of completing enough mileage in an F1 car to help him earn the much-desired super license. How He Got To 40 Points Finally For a driver to acquire an F1 super license, the FIA has set out different pointers. One of the key criteria is scoring 40 points, which is a combination of results from the three championships mentioned in the regulations. America’s IndyCar is part of that list, with F2 as well. Taking that into account, Herta had 35 points from the last three seasons of IndyCar he competed in. He required five more points, which he earned by undertaking five practice sessions. F1 allows additional super license points for taking part in FP1 sessions, which is one per session up to 10. Before Mexico , Herta completed FP1 sessions in Barcelona, Hungary, Italy and Austin to accumulate the five points he required. The one additional point is on the basis of completing 100 km during the FP1 session, which he fulfilled in the Mexico GP after his 24th lap of the 29 he did. He now has enough points to become a full-time F1 driver in 2027 if Cadillac wants to. item.title: Red Bull F1 boss Laurent Mekies hits back at Christian Horner's "lost its mojo" claim
item.description: Motorsport photo Red Bull Racing CEO and team principal Laurent Mekies has rejected Christian Horner's claim that the Milton Keynes outfit has "lost its mojo" since his exit, insisting its spirit has driven a "very remarkable" turnaround. Horner, who left the team in July 2025 after two decades in charge, has been promoting his memoir Drive , which was published last week. During an interview with The Times , the Briton claimed the team had "lost its mojo, its presence, its vibe" since he left. Asked about the comments in Friday's team principals' press conference in Mexico City, Mekies said: "Look, first of all, Christian is entitled to his opinion. He obviously has spent a lot of time in this team and I respect his point of view. "We certainly feel extremely differently about the vibe in the team. One of the strong points we have been enjoying certainly in the last few months is the incredible team spirit that has allowed us to come back from an objectively very difficult moment. Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing "It's always one thing to have a positive spirit when you are winning races, it's something else to have that same fighting spirit and unity between the team members when you are put under pressure, and we certainly had a challenging first part of the year, on the chassis side and the PU side. "The way the team stuck together, the way the team set the Milton Keynes department on fire to try to come back, and the way they have done that, it's such a challenging matter, from any of our team members to the brutally honest comments of our drivers. That's the Red Bull spirit and that's certainly how we feel we need to go racing. "The guys got the reward they deserved with the turnaround that they have produced, which is very remarkable, but ultimately we are well aware that we live and die with our results. "The target is not to win one race or two races; the target is to be back to world titles, and until we are there, nobody will feel we have achieved anything." item.description: FORT DODGE — Mary Grace Lyons achieved her dream a little sooner than expected.
